Entropy

Entropy estimates cell-level transcriptional entropy from single-cell expression data. Entropy is calculated across local cell neighborhoods and can be used to investigate transcriptional variability, cellular plasticity, and changes in cell identity.

Package documentation

Overview

The package provides count-based entropy estimation using the best upper bound (BUB) estimator and binary entropy estimation for presence/absence data. Analyses can be performed directly from either Seurat objects or AnnData .h5ad files.

Main capabilities include:

  • automatic PCA-based nearest-neighbor construction and custom neighbor input;
  • restriction of neighborhoods within biological or technical groups;
  • count-based and binary entropy estimation;
  • scoring of selected feature sets;
  • chunked and parallel computation for larger datasets;
  • per-cell summaries and optional gene-by-cell entropy output.

Installation 

devtools::install_gitlab(
  "grp-zaugg/entropy_package",
  host = "git.embl.de",
  force = TRUE
)

AnnData support

run_entropy_h5ad() provides direct support for AnnData .h5ad files without requiring conversion to a Seurat object. It reads expression data, dimensional reductions, and observation metadata while preserving AnnData cell and feature identifiers. Results are returned as per-cell values that can be joined to adata.obs.

Direct h5ad support requires R 4.5.0 or newer, anndataR 1.0.0 or newer, and rhdf5. Installation, data preparation, analysis options, result validation, and Scanpy visualization are described in the Python and AnnData workflow.
